title: Common Hackberry: Ancient Hackberries You Can Visit
meta_description: A tough North American shade tree. Cook County's champion stands 36.6 metres tall; Italy protects one in Padua for growing at an odd angle.
intro: The common hackberry is a tough tree of the American interior, warty-barked and planted for shade, rarely famous, which makes the ones that got noticed worth the walk. In the Forest Preserves of Cook County outside Chicago, the register's champion at Thatcher Woods stands 36.6 metres tall on a trunk 3.51 metres round, and the one at National Grove matches that girth to the centimetre. Utah's champion, at the corner of Washington Square in Salt Lake City, is wider than it is tall. In Minneapolis, students have been throwing tied pairs of shoes into one under the Washington Avenue Bridge since at least 1995. And in Padua, Italy put a middling hackberry on its national register for its shape: it leans, throwing its limbs out sideways and low over the grass of Parco Treves. Nobody has dated any of them.
